what_happened: The user corrected Athena's reading of a request in job 614b. The first reading did not cover a problem found by an earlier job's verifier (hem1). Unread requests were being refused and left in the queue forever. The user said the planning pass must read them so the drain can keep working the queue. The reading was corrected before the job went forward.
cause: Athena builds a reading from the request text alone. It does not pull in the open findings of the earlier job the request refers to, and it does not state what must be true of the queue afterwards (no item stuck unread, the drain still moving). The system therefore never tests a reading against the earlier verifier's unresolved findings or against a stated end state. The user's correction was the first check. This is not an ambiguous word or a presence-only criterion. The reading was incomplete about scope inherited from earlier work.
prevention: When a request refers to an earlier job or verifier, admission should load that job's unresolved blocker and major findings and require the reading to map each one to a deliverable or to an explicit exclusion. Admission should reject the reading if any finding is unmapped. For queue work, the reading should also include an observable acceptance criterion: no item stays queued and unread, and the drain completes with such an item present.
proposed_request: Fix the queue so that a request that has not been read is never refused and left queued forever. The planning pass must read it, so the drain can still work through the queue. This also covers the unresolved findings from hem1's verifier. Acceptance: with an unread request in the queue, a drain run reads it in planning and moves it forward, and no request stays queued unread. Add a test that runs the drain with an unread request present and shows the queue empties or advances.
